_about: Description-shaped recall. Every case below is a REAL question asked during
live dogfooding on 2026-08-21, against a repository Icarus had just indexed,
and every gold ref was confirmed present in the fixture corpus before being
The property under test is NOT honesty. Both live misses abstained or
answered from lesser evidence rather than bluffing, and the gate never passed
a false claim. The property is RECALL: an agent about to do work asks in
prose, never by identifier, so evidence reachable only by number is evidence
the product cannot deliver on the journey it advertises.
`phrasing` is the axis: `identifier` names the ref outright, `task` describes
the work in the repository's own vocabulary, `intent` asks what the caller
actually wants to know and shares no vocabulary with the evidence at all.

cases.question: What does issue 841 say about rows_where and delete_where?
cases.note: The control. Exact-identifier lookup is the path measured to work, and it is what makes the misses below a ranking result rather than an ingest result: the evidence is provably in the corpus.

cases.question: Should I fix rows_where and delete_where to raise an error on a non-existent table?
cases.note: The question an agent asks before starting the work. Retrieval ranks issue:841 first here -- yet the LIVE brain answered from issue:315 and db.py and never surfaced the maintainer's instruction, so the failure on this case is downstream of retrieval. Kept as a guard: if this ever stops ranking, the harder cases below cannot be diagnosed.

cases.question: Is there any work the maintainer has asked contributors not to do?
cases.note: THE RED CASE. simonw wrote on issue 841: 'So don't let your agent work on this, I'll do this if and when 5 becomes a thing in the future.' Nothing in the code or git log records it. The question shares no vocabulary with the evidence -- no method name, no issue number -- which is exactly how a caller asks when they do not already know the answer.

cases.question: Which planned changes are being held back for a future major version?
cases.note: Same evidence, a second intent-shaped phrasing, so one lucky or unlucky wording cannot decide the measurement. issue:841 states the change is held for v5.

cases.question: Does delete_where commit its changes in the 3.x series?
cases.note: A second real case from the same session, with a different gold ref, so the board does not rest on one issue. issue:815 records that the 3.x commit bug is fixed in 4.0 and deserves a dot-release backport.
